A conntrack-tracking Linux router on commodity hardware handles roughly 1-3 Mpps per core.
The packet rate a Linux router forwards per core depends on CPU, NIC, driver and ruleset and has to be measured.
At 1 Gb/s, 64-byte frames give about 1,488,095 packets per second.
At 10 Gb/s, 64-byte frames give about 1.49 Mpps.
Every frame occupies 20 extra bytes on the wire: 8 of preamble and 12 of inter-frame gap.
The inter-frame gap is 12 bytes and there is no preamble on the wire.
A 1518-byte frame at 10 Gb/s gives about 812,744 packets per second.
